newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business confidence slipped in Q3-Conf Board.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business confidence slipped in Q3-Conf Board.

text.p: The Conference Board's measure of U.S. business confidence among chief executives fell two points to 53 in the third-quarter of 1996 versus 55 in the second-quarter, the organization said on Wednesday.
Company leaders were slightly more positive about the current economy, but somewhat less positive about conditions in their own industries, the survey said.

"Business executives' outlook for the economy during the next six months is less optimistic than in the second quarter of the year," concluded Lynn Franco associate director of The Conference Board's Consumer Research Center.
The percentage of executives who feel conditions have worsened over the past six months decreased to about 20 percent from 25 percent.

According to the survey, business leaders' outlook for their own industries is brighter than in the second quarter. More than 37 percent predict improving conditions and 20 percent look for worsening conditions.
The Conference Board's barometer is based on a quarterly survey of more than 200 chief executives and other business leaders representing a wide variety of industries.
"About one out of every four CEOs anticipates a pickup in overall economic activity, down from almost one out of three in the second quarter," Franco added.
About 43 percent of those surveyed said economic conditions in general are better than six months ago, up from 41 percent last quarter.
But less than 40 percent said conditions in their own industries have improved versus 43 percent in the second quarter. -- Caryn Trokie, 212 859-1678
